best_for: People who need to lock down a laptop drive, a USB stick or a folder of files with open-source encryption they can move between Windows, Mac and Linux.

points.title: Containers, drives or the whole system
points.text: You can make an encrypted file container that mounts as a drive, encrypt a USB stick or partition, or encrypt the Windows system drive with a password asked before Windows starts.

points.title: Hidden volumes for deniability
points.text: A hidden volume can sit inside another encrypted volume, and Windows can run a hidden operating system. If someone forces you to give up a password, you can reveal the outer one.

points.title: Old TrueCrypt files need 1.25.9
points.text: VeraCrypt is based on TrueCrypt 7.1a, but current releases point TrueCrypt-format users to the older VeraCrypt 1.25.9. Convert old containers with that version first.

points.title: Macs need a FUSE layer
points.text: Current builds need macOS Monterey 12 or later, and you choose a download for macFUSE or for FUSE-T. The project suggests FUSE-T on Apple silicon Macs. Install the FUSE layer that matches the build you download.

points.title: Free, with ARM64 and portable builds
points.text: It costs nothing, and VeraCrypt's own download page also offers ARM64 installers and a portable Windows exe. The Windows listing here keeps 9 versions as a 64-bit machine-wide installer; macOS lists only the current universal dmg, so older Mac builds need another source.

points.title: Linux packages come from the project
points.text: The download page has AppImage, .deb and .rpm builds for current Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and openSUSE releases, plus Raspberry Pi builds. Linux is not listed on this site.
